subject: Upgrade decision help — feature vs throughput tradeoffs
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@orthohealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: OrthoHealth Procurement <procurement@orthohealth.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Upgrade options — need simple decision matrix

Hi Hannah,

We're looking at shifting from your Compact tier to something that gives us better peak throughput for our weekend surge, while keeping the feature set (function calling + streaming) intact. Our usage profile is highly spiky: 70% normal traffic, 30% concentrated weekend bursts.

Questions:
- Is there a straightforward way to compare expected per-token costs vs. effective latency for the Compact+Burst vs. Tier B (flat) options?
- What features are gated on the higher tiers (are there any hidden entitlements we need)?
- We may pursue an annual commit if the economics work — can you share a decision matrix we can run against our usage CSV?

I attached a small sample of last month's traffic for context (current-usage.csv). Looking for something concise we can bring to procurement.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Engineering
OrthoHealth
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@orthohealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Upgrade options — need simple decision matrix

Hi Samir — thanks for the data, very helpful.

Short answer up-front: yes — we can model both per-token economics and latency impact. I put together a simple decision matrix (upgrade-decision-matrix-v1.xlsx) that shows:
- Expected monthly cost at your current shape + surge profile
- Token-latency tradeoff estimates per route (function calls are slightly higher CPU)
- Feature entitlements per tier (streaming, function calling, fine-grained routing)

High-level recommendations:
- If your weekend spikes are predictable, Compact + Burst is usually cheaper (burst credit pricing) and preserves feature entitlements.
- If you need consistent SLA during peaks or want simplified billing, Tier B (flat) reduces variance but costs more at steady-state.

Can we do a 30-minute run-through tomorrow to walk the matrix against your CSV and run a quick sensitivity? Marissa from Sales will join to outline pricing scenarios.

Attachment: upgrade-decision-matrix-v1.xlsx (matrix + example scenarios)

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@orthohealth.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Upgrade options — need simple decision matrix

Thanks Hannah — adding a few pricing notes so procurement has clarity.

Samir, quick bullets on commercial choices:
- Option A: Compact + Burst credits — lower committed monthly spend, burst credits apply to weekend surges. Good if spikes are short and predictable.
- Option B: Tier B (flat) — higher baseline but guarantees capacity and removes burst accounting; includes streaming + function calling by default.
- Discounting: For annual commits we can provide a tiered discount (5–15% depending on commit size); for this deal I'm proposing a 10% introductory discount on Tier B if OrthoHealth signs a 12-month commitment and allows Redwood to run a 60-day pilot for performance validation.

I've attached our latest pricing workbook (pricing-matrix-v2.xlsx) and a draft SOW for the pilot (SOW-draft-orthohealth.pdf). Rishi — can you confirm approval on the 10% proposal and pilot terms?

Next step: If that looks reasonable, I'll prepare a concise commercial summary for procurement and a DocuSign SOW link.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir@orthohealth.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Upgrade options — need simple decision matrix

Marissa — approved with conditions.

Approval: 10% discount on Tier B for a 12-month annual commitment, conditional on:
- A 60-day pilot window where Redwood must meet the agreed latency targets (SLO: p95 inference latency <= 220ms for the main route).
- Usage telemetry shared during the pilot (we need basic token / route breakdown).
- Single renewal clause at 12 months with standard price-step increase capped at 5% unless material change in aggregate throughput.

Procurement: we should include a one-time migration assistance credit (40 hours) to help move routing and prefix caching settings. Please add that to the SOW.

Marissa — please prepare the commercial summary and include the DocuSign SOW link. Samir — if those terms look ok I can sign off and we can route to legal for standard redlines.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Samir Patel <samir@orthohealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 09:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Upgrade options — need simple decision matrix

Thanks — that structure looks good to us. A few quick requests before procurement routes this internally:
- Can you include an explicit rollback plan in the SOW in case the pilot doesn't meet the p95 SLO (we prefer a pilot clause that allows us to revert to Compact with pro-rated billing).
- Please add the migration assistance hours into the SOW as a line item credit.
- DocuSign link would be great so procurement has something to route.

If you can get the commercial summary + DocuSign by end of day, we'll start the internal approval.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to the trial.

Best,
Samir
Head of Platform Engineering, OrthoHealth
